name: Numbered method steps across a ground change
useWhen: Three or four named stages, each needing a sentence of substance rather than a label.
$useWhenNote: Written by hand, on purpose. Generating this line from family+form+arity produces the same boilerplate the old SNIPPET-INDEX descriptions already are ('three columns, dot headers') — construction, not the problem it solves. It is the only field here that cannot be derived, and the only one anyone reads when choosing.

focal.note: The reason this is not the same template as a numbered column list with a small ordinal. Bank slides 86 and 103 share family, form and near-arity and are compositionally opposite purely on this ratio: 86 runs 3.0, 103 runs 0.5 and the numeral becomes a label. No skeleton axis separates them.

replacesNote: columns-v5 covers the same content signal and loses the device: no ground change, numerals at an inline-overridden 120px in Thin, and the lower third of the canvas unused. Do not retire it until this template has been through a real deck.

deviations.why: RESOLVED in the frame-constants commit, but not to the measured 61. The brand playbook's Layout page states it literally for this exact canvas: 'Our most used format uses 40px square grid using 40px margins and 40px column space.' Brand-declared beats measured practice, so --m-edge is 40 and MAP's deeper text edge is available as --m-text:56px when a column of running copy needs it.

STILL OPEN. 64px is the 32pt source at the corrected x2 factor; the shell's 54px descends from the old x1.5. Rescaling the whole type scale is a bigger judgement than a frame constant and wants the tracer plus a human eye, so it was deliberately left out of the frame commit.

contractGapsClosed: .slide--ground — a partial-height ground change with a --ground-y split. .slide--white repaints the whole slide and could not express this.
.hero-num--m (192px, the measured tier) and .hero-num--solid (Regular). Added to build_shell.py rather than inlined, which is how columns-v5 got a 120px numeral fighting its own 144px class.
